name: Ecosystems & Biomes

objectives.text: Identify the living and nonliving parts of a schoolyard, garden, or farm habitat
Sort local plants and animals by the habitat where they live
Explain how a body feature or behavior helps a plant or animal survive in its habitat
Describe how a habitat provides food, water, shelter, and space for the living things in it
Describe how a change to a habitat such as drought, flooding, or plowing affects the organisms that live there
Locate the major land biomes of the world on a map and name the biome of the local area
Compare the plants and animals found in two different biomes, such as forest and grassland
Explain how latitude, elevation, temperature, and precipitation patterns determine where biomes occur
Distinguish among organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems, and biomes as levels of ecological organization
Describe the stages of ecological succession that follow a disturbance such as a wildfire or an abandoned crop field
Explain how competition, predation, mutualism, parasitism, and commensalism shape the community within an ecosystem
Interpret a climatogram to predict the biome of a location
Classify a given ecosystem by its climate, soil, and dominant vegetation to identify its biome
Identify the abiotic characteristics such as soil type, climate, and topography that define a local ecosystem
Describe the characteristics of rangeland and grassland biomes and the ecosystem services they provide to agriculture and society
Analyze how limiting factors such as water, temperature, and predation determine which organisms can survive in a biome
Apply the concept of carrying capacity to determine an appropriate stocking rate for a pasture or range unit
Explain the concept of landscape ecology and summarize how composition, structure, and function shape a farm or ranch landscape
Describe how indicator organisms such as macroinvertebrates and amphibians are used to assess the condition of an ecosystem
Evaluate the interdependence of biotic and abiotic components in a local agricultural or natural ecosystem
Compare natural ecosystems with agroecosystems such as cropland and pasture in structure, function, and stability
Assess the status of an ecosystem by surveying the trees, herbaceous plants, wildlife, and insects present, including native and invasive species
Interpret field signs of habitat disturbance and resilience to judge the health of an ecosystem
Evaluate a habitat site to determine its ecological quality and whether it is threatened, as in an FFA natural resources career development event
Evaluate how a change in climate or land use would shift the boundary between two neighboring biomes
Create an ecosystem management plan for a farm, ranch, or SAE property that sustains production while enhancing ecosystem function through native plant diversity

changes: Kept all six original objectives as real competencies and anchored the grade 10 and 12 ones to NRS.01.01.02.c. Filled gaps across the span: living and nonliving habitat parts, adaptations, habitat change, biome mapping, climate controls on biomes, levels of organization, succession, species interactions, and climatogram interpretation in the lower grades. Added high school objectives tied to AFNR standards on abiotic characteristics, rangeland ecosystem services, landscape ecology, bioindicators, biotic and abiotic interdependence, ecosystem status surveys, disturbance and resilience, and habitat evaluation for FFA CDE work, plus carrying capacity and stocking rate, natural versus agroecosystem comparison, and a culminating SAE management plan. Left soil microbe, carbon cycling, and biodiversity-focused standards to the Nutrient Cycles and Biodiversity siblings.
